newsitem.title: FRANCE: De Silguy says stability pact cannot be delayed.
newsitem.headline: De Silguy says stability pact cannot be delayed.

text.p: European Monetary Affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy said on Tuesday it was important not to delay agreement on the stability pact aimed at policing budget discipline after introduction of the euro.
Asked on French Radio Inter whether he believed agreement on the stability pact could be reached at next week's Amsterdam EU summit, de Silguy replied, "We must have an agreement now."
He said a delay would give a "backward signal" on monetary union.
But French European Affairs Minister Pierre Moscovici said on Monday that the stability pact could not be approved at the Amsterdam summit.
He said that the new French government needed more time to evaluate the contents of the pact, negotiated by its centre-right predecessors, and to press for additional clauses.
The June 16-17 Amsterdam summit had been due to formally approve the pact to be signed by ministers afterwards.
De Silguy said that the European Union had laid down objectives which it would achieve according to a timetable.
"It is important to maintain this timetable. If not, it would a backwards signal and very damaging for everyone and for France in particular," he said.

France has said it wants to add to clauses to the pact, one enshrining coordination of economic polcies among EU member states through an "economic government" and the other setting out a European ggrowth initiative to promote employment.
The new French government has insisted it is committed to launching the euro on time in 1999 and meeting the Maastricht treaty conditions for monetary union.
